question: Are customers describing the same underlying problem in different ways?

answer.answer_markdown:
**Yes, and to a degree that breaks keyword reporting: the single largest theme in the book covers 407 contacts that customers wrote 417 different ways, with almost no vocabulary in common.**

The theme is "unexplained account closures or restrictions" - 7.5% of everything in scope, across 7 products. Three of its members, all from different products and months, share no searchable words at all. One customer writes "I called Chase customer service and was informed that my account had been closed without prior notification." A second, on a mortgage, writes "my agreed upon payment would not be accepted because of potential fraud and equity theft". A third, on a wire, writes "In this call, I passed the security review, yet I was given a reason that my fund was insufficient. My wire was hence cancelled." A fourth, chasing an auto payoff, writes only "Chase refused to give me that information." No search for "account closed" finds the last three; no search for "wire" finds the first. They are the same operational failure: a risk control fired and nobody would say why.

It is not one outlier theme. The second-biggest cluster, fraud and dispute claims denied despite evidence, holds 396 calls in 398 distinct wordings over 7 products and 42 states - the wording ranges from a formal "I am writing to formally dispute your denial of my claim" to a customer simply saying the item arrived damaged and the merchant would not answer. Across the whole book, 7,417 extracted issue statements collapse into 227 active themes, and the fifteen themes with the widest vocabulary alone account for 2,188 calls.

The practical consequence is a sizing error, not a reporting nicety. Anything counted by keyword, canned reason code or agent disposition splits these into dozens of small, ignorable buckets. Grouped by meaning, two of them are each a 400-contact problem - large enough to fund a fix, and each pointing at a single root cause: risk models that restrict or deny without an explanation the front line is allowed to give.

quotes.quote: I called Chase customer service and was informed that my account had been closed without prior notification.
quotes.why: Plain wording: the account was simply closed with no notice.

quotes.quote: my agreed upon payment would not be accepted because of potential fraud and equity theft
quotes.why: Same theme, no shared keywords: a mortgage payment refused over a fraud suspicion.

quotes.quote: In this call, I passed the security review, yet I was given a reason that my fund was insufficient. My wire was hence cancelled.
quotes.why: Same theme again: a wire cancelled for a reason the customer knows is false.

quotes.quote: Chase refused to give me that information.
quotes.why: Same theme, four words: the bank will not say.

quotes.quote: I have never committed fraud or any illegal activity on these accounts or any money laundering. I asked for a reason and they wouldn't tell me anything. They just closed the accounts.
quotes.why: The shared core the three above never spell out: no reason given.

quotes.quote: I have tried to get Chase to correct their mistake, even taking it up to the executive office, but they continue to say they have " no proof '' that I was assured no reporting to my credit.
quotes.why: Denial theme, mortgage credit reporting wording.

quotes.quote: I did receive the item, but it was damaged and I tried to contact the merchant to no avail. That's why I disputed the charge.
quotes.why: Same denial theme in a phone call about a damaged item.

quotes.quote: Chase declined to assist and directed me back to the repossession company, despite the repossession company acting on their behalf.
quotes.why: Same denial theme, wording about a repossession company.

caveats: Unfiltered scope mixes two corpora: 4,425 real written CFPB complaints about one bank (July 2024 to June 2026) and 1,000 synthetic phone conversations from September 2023. Written complaints are longer and more varied than spoken calls, so some of the wording spread reflects the channel.
A wording is one extracted issue statement per contact, so the count is bounded by theme size; it measures how differently the problem is phrased, not how often it recurs.
The grouping is model-made. Themes flagged as weakly grouped are excluded from these rankings, but a small number of members in any theme may be misplaced.
Quotes are verbatim and redaction markers (XXXX) come from the source complaints.

payload.name: list_themes
payload.summary: 15 rows over 5425 calls in scope; Unexplained account closures or restrictions (407), Fraud and dispute claims denied despite evidence (396), Contradictory information from bank representatives (383)

sql.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(c.date) AS d0, MAX(c.date) AS d1 FROM calls c WHERE 1=1

SELECT th.theme_id, th.name, th.problem_statement, th.root_cause, th.polarity, th.driver_category, th.n_wordings, th.n_products, COALESCE(th.grouping_quality, 'ok') AS grouping_quality, th.first_seen_week, es.status AS status_at_as_of, es.emerging_score, COUNT(DISTINCT s.call_id) AS n_calls, SUM(CASE WHEN s.min_sentiment < 0 THEN -s.min_sentiment ELSE 0 END) AS neg_mass, SUM(CASE WHEN s.max_sentiment > 0 THEN s.max_sentiment ELSE 0 END) AS pos_mass, AVG(CASE WHEN th.polarity = 'positive' THEN s.max_sentiment ELSE s.min_sentiment END) AS mean_sentiment FROM themes th JOIN v_theme_call_sentiment s ON s.theme_id = th.theme_id JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = s.call_id LEFT JOIN emerging_scores es ON es.entity_type = 'theme' AND es.entity_id = th.theme_id AND es.as_of_week = ? WHERE 1=1 AND th.status = 'active' AND COALESCE(th.grouping_quality, 'ok') != 'weak' GROUP BY th.theme_id HAVING n_calls >= ? ORDER BY th.n_wordings DESC, th.theme_id LIMIT ?
SELECT tc.theme_id, tc.call_id FROM v_theme_calls tc JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = tc.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND tc.theme_id IN (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?) ORDER BY c.date DESC, tc.call_id

SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(c.date) AS d0, MAX(c.date) AS d1 FROM calls c WHERE 1=1

SELECT e.evidence_id, e.call_id, c.date, c.month, c.product, c.region, c.region_group, c.channel, c.segment, t.sentiment, e.quote, e.speaker, t.topic_label, t.driver, e.char_start, e.char_end, e.match_kind FROM evidence e JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id = e.topic_id JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = e.call_id JOIN theme_members tm ON tm.topic_id = t.topic_id WHERE e.verified = 1 AND tm.effective_theme_id = ? AND 1=1 ORDER BY ABS(t.sentiment) DESC, c.date DESC, e.evidence_id
